metadata.research_goal: Create backend-ready records for cycling beginner, intermediate, and advanced level assessment, progression gates, hold/regression rules, and auto-with-review recommendations.
metadata.write_scope: single draft file for cycling level assessment and teaching progression only
metadata.synthesis_note: Records combine handling readiness, endurance markers, power/HR/RPE availability, discipline context, pain response, and training consistency.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling level should be treated as a recommendation state, not a fixed identity.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store evidence and review status when recommending beginner to intermediate or intermediate to advanced movement.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling level has two axes: physical training capacity and bike-handling/road-readiness.
key_concepts.backend_use: A user may have strong aerobic fitness but still remain beginner for outdoor cycling skills.

key_concepts.concept: Power, HR, cadence, and route data improve precision, but RPE and completion history are enough for safe beginner plans.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not block planning when FTP or power meter data are absent.

key_concepts.concept: A rider can be intermediate on an indoor trainer and beginner in MTB, group riding, or criterium contexts.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store level by discipline or context when possible.

key_concepts.concept: Progression should require stable or improving pain and contact-point response, not only better fitness.
key_concepts.backend_use: Hold level progression when knee, back, neck, hand, saddle, calf, or Achilles symptoms worsen.

key_concepts.concept: Group riding readiness depends on line holding, braking, signaling, proximity comfort, and predictability.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not unlock fast group rides based only on FTP or endurance.

key_concepts.concept: Advanced cycling should be discipline-specific: road racing, TT, MTB, BMX, track, gravel, and triathlon all need different progressions.
key_concepts.backend_use: Advanced unlocks should require discipline context and not just high training volume.

key_concepts.concept: If recovery, sleep, fueling, or completion are poor, the plan should hold or regress even when fitness markers improve.
key_concepts.backend_use: Level recommendations should integrate completion, RPE drift, soreness, pain, and fatigue.

technical_models.name: Cycling level matrix
technical_models.backend_use: Recommend level from multiple signals instead of one FTP or weekly volume number.

technical_models.name: Beginner to intermediate gate
technical_models.backend_use: Auto-with-review recommendation: ready for intermediate cycling foundation.

technical_models.name: Intermediate to advanced gate
requirements: can complete threshold/tempo work without pain spikes
technical_models.backend_use: Auto-with-review recommendation: ready for advanced discipline-specific block.

technical_models.name: Hold or regress gate
conditions: missed rides after illness or crash
technical_models.backend_use: Keep current level or temporarily regress training complexity.

technical_models.name: FTP and power readiness model
technical_models.backend_use: Use FTP testing only when useful and safe; otherwise estimate with RPE/HR/session history.

technical_models.name: Contextual advanced unlock
technical_models.backend_use: Store separate readiness flags per discipline/context.

technical_models.name: Group ride readiness model
technical_models.backend_use: Gate fast group rides, pacelines, and criterium tactics.

tactical_rules.rule: Advance cycling level only when completion, symptom response, handling readiness, and training tolerance support the change.
Strong gym or running fitness does not automatically unlock advanced outdoor cycling environments.
FTP or hard power testing should wait until the rider has consistent cycling sessions and can pace safely.
Beginner riders should not stack long rides, hills, hard intervals, and heavy lower-body gym work in the same microcycle.
Intermediate riders may receive tempo or threshold work when easy ride completion, pain response, and recovery are stable.
Advanced riders should receive discipline-specific intensity and tactics rather than generic harder cycling.
Worsening pain, contact-point symptoms, crash history, or high fatigue overrides level progression.
tactical_rules.backend_trigger: pain_trend = worsening OR crash_recent = true OR fatigue_high = true

tactical_rules.rule: Use separate readiness states for indoor cycling, outdoor road, group riding, MTB/off-road, racing, and triathlon cycling.
After illness, crash, or a long break, reduce level complexity temporarily even if the user was previously advanced.
tactical_rules.backend_trigger: break_days >= 14 OR illness_recent = true OR crash_recent = true

tactical_rules.rule: If power/HR data are noisy or missing, use RPE, completion, route context, and recovery response for progression decisions.

physical_demands.advanced_marker: event-specific long rides or high-quality intervals with recovery

physical_demands.intermediate_marker: group basics, hills, descending, predictable braking
physical_demands.advanced_marker: discipline-specific cornering, descending, pack, off-road, or race tactics
uses cadence strategically for terrain and event demands

physical_demands.beginner_marker: no symptom spikes after easy rides
physical_demands.intermediate_marker: recovers from moderate intervals and long rides

physical_demands.advanced_marker: tolerates aero, race, off-road, or high-speed positions

physical_demands.beginner_marker: hydrates and eats normally around short rides

injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Hold or regress level recommendation until symptoms stabilize.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: using FTP as the only measure of cycling level
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Require handling, recovery, completion, and discipline context.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: VO2, anaerobic, or sprint work before base and safety
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Keep beginner plans mostly easy with short controlled skill exposures.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: joining fast group rides before handling readiness
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Require group ride skill assessment and start with slower/no-drop contexts.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: using road cycling readiness to unlock MTB, BMX, track, or criterium demands
commuting, work stress, and poor sleep masking overload
returning at previous level after a break
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Use return-to-ride block and lower complexity until tolerance returns.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: cycling-only progression without strength or mobility support
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Add trunk, hip, lower-limb, and posture support, especially for intermediate and advanced riders.

training_implications.implication: Beginner cycling sessions should include teaching intent, not just minutes on bike.
training_implications.backend_use: Generate skill-focused sessions like braking, shifting, quiet-route practice, and cadence comfort.

training_implications.implication: Intermediate cycling sessions should introduce structured endurance, tempo, and threshold while preserving recovery.
training_implications.backend_use: Use zones/RPE and progress one variable at a time.

training_implications.implication: Advanced cycling sessions should map to discipline and event demands.
training_implications.backend_use: Retrieve discipline-specific tactical and physical records before generation.

training_implications.implication: Level review should occur after a meaningful training sample, not every session.
training_implications.backend_use: Review every 4 weeks or after 8-12 ride completions.

training_implications.implication: Handling confidence can lag behind fitness and may need its own progressions.
training_implications.backend_use: Separate handling skill flags from endurance level.

training_implications.implication: A beginner without power, HR, or cadence sensors can still receive high-quality plans.
training_implications.backend_use: Use RPE, route, duration, completion, and symptoms.

training_implications.implication: The next block should use recent completion, RPE, pain, and long-ride response.
training_implications.backend_use: Persist athlete_state and update after daily snapshots.

training_implications.implication: Level progression should modify the macro plan rather than rewrite it randomly.
training_implications.backend_use: Use macro block theme plus athlete_state to choose progression or hold.

training_implications.implication: A rider can remain beginner for road/traffic while becoming intermediate for indoor fitness.
Advanced work may require power meter, safe route, trainer, bike type, or discipline-specific equipment.
training_implications.backend_use: Gate advanced sessions by equipment and environment.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling beginner to intermediate
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Eligible after 4+ consistent weeks or 8+ completed rides, 85% completion, stable pain, easy ride duration tolerance, and basic handling readiness.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling intermediate to advanced
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Eligible after 8+ additional consistent weeks, stable progression, controlled tempo/threshold tolerance, discipline-specific skill readiness, and recovery support.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling hold or regress
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Hold or regress when completion is low, pain worsens, fatigue is high, RPE overshoots, crash/illness occurred, or handling confidence is low.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling handling readiness
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Assess start/stop, braking, turning, scanning, signaling, shifting, line holding, and comfort near hazards.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling group ride readiness
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Assess line holding, predictable braking, signaling, shoulder checking, proximity comfort, etiquette, and no-drop ride completion.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling intensity readiness
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Assess ride consistency, RPE control, HR/power availability, fatigue response, and ability to complete tempo work without symptom spikes.

backend_records_to_create.name: Contextual cycling level
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Store separate readiness for indoor, outdoor road, group riding, MTB/off-road, racing, and triathlon cycling.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling auto-with-review assessment
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: current_level, recommended_level, context, evidence, risks, missing_evidence, review_status, next_review_date.

backend_records_to_create.name: Power data optional for beginner cycling
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Use RPE, route, duration, completion, and symptoms when power/HR data are absent or unreliable.

backend_records_to_create.name: FTP testing readiness gate
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Only test FTP after consistent cycling history, safe test context, stable fatigue, and ability to pace hard efforts.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling beginner foundation block
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Control skills, short easy rides, flat/quiet route progression, contact-point monitoring, and strength support.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling intermediate build block
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Longer endurance ride, cadence drills, tempo/threshold exposure, route-specific skill, and recovery monitoring.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling advanced discipline block
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Discipline-specific intensity, terrain simulation, tactical practice, event fueling, and taper rules.
